title: Preserving muscle in MVA
status: Niacin-priority review revision; no Track 2 portal submission; public Vimeo V2 at https://vimeo.com/1228990028 serves this revision with current English captions, verified 21 September 2026

slides.title:
Preserving muscle
in MVA
slides.narration: This child has muscle wasting and mosaic variegated aneuploidy, a condition in which cells can carry different numbers of chromosomes. Our question is whether an existing medicine could improve muscle function while preserving the cells needed for growth and repair. We propose two medicines for laboratory testing.

slides.title: Protein supply is a testable mechanism
slides.narration: Bub one B makes the checkpoint protein Bub R one. Our stop-plus-missense pair matches a reported MVA one pattern: reduced protein supply. The missense protein's stability and function remain unmeasured. Trans phase needs confirmation. Confirmed cis retires this pair as the compound-heterozygous explanation.

slides.title: Niacin tests usable protein restoration
slides.narration: Niacin is our lead because it targets the protein-supply hypothesis. It raised muscle N A D in another myopathy. Separate experiments connect N A D and SIRT two to Bub R one stability. Niacin has not rescued this genotype. We test whether it increases usable protein and useful muscle.

slides.title: Everolimus is a downstream probe
slides.narration: Everolimus is our downstream probe. It inhibits em tor complex one, a growth pathway. A small carrier-mouse blot showed stronger phosphoprotein bands, without quantified pathway activity. Rapamycin preserved stem-cell numbers in a different fly model. Neither establishes muscle rescue. We require functional benefit with preserved growth and renewal.

slides.title: Cell selection and tissue output
slides.narration: Our cell-selection explorer exposes a misleading result. In one simulated scenario, the chromosome-normal fraction rose sixteen point eight percentage points while total differentiated-cell time fell eleven percent. Other teams can inspect this tradeoff across declared assumptions. Our proposed experiment tracks starting cells, including those that die or stop dividing.

slides.title: The experiment must show useful muscle
slides.narration: We would compare affected and genetically corrected muscle models, using measured drug exposures. A medicine must improve either existing muscle or new muscle production, preserve the other, and avoid worsening chromosome errors. Independent confirmation must reproduce the result. The cancer history also requires checking that neither medicine helps tumor cells survive or interferes with cancer treatment.

slides.title: Other routes have defined tests for advancement
slides.narration: Arimoclomol remains a reserve because rescue of this protein is unproved. Removing senescent cells has strong genetic mouse evidence, but some drugs also damage repair in young muscle. We investigate that mechanism in parallel. Transcript rescue and other alternatives have explicit promotion tests in our report.

slides.title: Public reuse and the next experiment
slides.narration: We also ran the workflow on a public, synthetic TRIP thirteen example. It shows why a Bub R one restoration hypothesis cannot simply transfer to another gene. That demonstrates reuse, not treatment validation. Next we need a consented muscle model and laboratory partner to test niacin, with everolimus as comparator.
